entries.clue: Everything is a burden, it’s said unfailingly (6)

indicatorNotes.it’s said: what is said is heard, not read, so the sound counts rather than the spelling

annotation.surface: Someone sighing that life, every bit of it, is a weight to carry.
annotation.walkthrough: Say ALL WEIGHS quickly and you hear ALWAYS; the sound covers the whole phrase, not just the second word.
annotation.definitionFit: Unfailingly means at all times, which is always.

entries.clue: Glad eye? Wind-up! (4)

indicatorNotes.up: in a down entry, up means the letters read from the bottom

blocks.note: to reel in a line is to wind it

annotation.surface: A flirtatious look that turns out to be a tease.
annotation.walkthrough: Wind-up reads as one word meaning a joke at someone’s expense; split it and it becomes the instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: The glad eye is a suggestive look, and a leer is a knowing, suggestive look; the question mark flags the loose fit.

entries.clue: Norman Tebbit’s role – to have a go at setter? (6,3)

blocks.note: to have a go at someone is to attack them
a setter is a breed of gundog

annotation.surface: A question about the politician Norman Tebbit and whether he would turn on the puzzle’s own compiler.
annotation.walkthrough: The setter here is not Brummie but the gundog. Norman Tebbit was a combative Conservative minister, known as Margaret Thatcher’s attack dog.
annotation.definitionFit: An attack dog is a politician deployed to savage opponents, the job Tebbit did for Thatcher.

entries.clue: Abandons theatre wear (6)

blocks.note: to scrub a plan is to drop it
the loose garments worn in an operating theatre

annotation.surface: An actor walking out of the costume department.
annotation.walkthrough: Theatre suggests the stage; in Britain it is also the hospital operating theatre, where surgeons wear scrubs.
annotation.definitionFit: Scrubs as a verb means cancels or abandons; as a noun it is surgical clothing.

entries.clue: Bat’s preparatory move, dramatically illuminated when female enters (8)

indicatorNotes.enters: the female goes into the other word

blocks.note: lit from behind, as on a stage

annotation.surface: A night-time scene of a bat caught in stage lighting as a female flies in.
annotation.walkthrough: Bat looks like the flying animal; it is the cricket bat. The backlift is how a batsman raises the bat before a stroke.
annotation.definitionFit: The backlift is the upward movement of the bat that prepares a cricket shot.

entries.clue: Cheap gibes at barman ineptly carrying measure (7-8)

indicatorNotes.ineptly: done ineptly, the letters end up in the wrong order
indicatorNotes.carrying: the anagram holds the measure inside it

blocks.note: an en is a printer’s measure of width

annotation.surface: Customers mocking a bartender while he clumsily pours a drink.
annotation.walkthrough: The anagram of the thirteen letters gives BARGAINBASEMT, and EN goes in near the end.
annotation.definitionFit: Bargain-basement goods are the cheapest, from the discount floor of a store.

entries.clue: Scam merchant gets rid of diamonds for union official (8)

indicatorNotes.gets rid of: whatever the merchant gets rid of, here the diamonds, is thrown out of the word

blocks.note: D = diamonds, the card suit; this is the letter removed

annotation.surface: A fraudster jettisoning stolen gems to pass as a trade union man.
annotation.walkthrough: A convenor is a British trade union term for the official who calls meetings and leads shop stewards.
annotation.definitionFit: A convenor is an elected union official who organises members at a workplace.

entries.clue: Bar entrance – strip clubs inside (5)

blocks.note: a lath is a thin strip of wood

annotation.surface: A bouncer’s view of a strip club, with the bar entrance just inside.
annotation.walkthrough: Bar entrance reads as the way into a pub; it is an instruction, to bar an entrance, which is what you do when you latch a door.
annotation.definitionFit: To latch is to fasten a door, barring the entrance.

entries.clue: Serious affair? No, not if trial’s rigged (10)

indicatorNotes.rigged: a rigged trial is one rearranged to order

annotation.surface: A courtroom remark that a case can only go one way if the trial is fixed.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition runs to the No: a flirtation is an affair that is not serious. The comma hides where it stops.
annotation.definitionFit: A flirtation is a light romantic dalliance, the opposite of a serious affair.

entries.clue: Stop working with rock star’s ultimate fixer (8)

indicatorNotes.ultimate: the ultimate letter is the last one

blocks.note: to rest is to stop working

annotation.surface: Someone downing tools to go and join a rock star’s crew.
annotation.walkthrough: Rock star looks like one phrase; rock is ORE and star only supplies its last letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A restorer repairs old things, so is a fixer.

entries.clue: Explosive agent and critic put off introducing one (6,4)

indicatorNotes.put off: put off its stride, the phrase is thrown into disorder
indicatorNotes.introducing: the phrase takes the one into it

annotation.surface: A saboteur and a reviewer are put off their stride by a newcomer.
annotation.walkthrough: The word and is not a link here; its three letters are part of the fodder. The answer runs on into 13 across.
annotation.definitionFit: Nitric acid is used to make explosives such as nitroglycerine and TNT.

entries.clue: Many a flutter initiated by this US money (and a bit English) (7,5)

indicatorNotes.initiated by: the answer starts with what follows

blocks.note: cabbage is American slang for money
a whit is a tiny bit

annotation.surface: A gambler admitting that most bets are funded with dollars, plus a little sterling.
annotation.walkthrough: Flutter suggests a small bet, and US money fits that picture; but the flutter is a butterfly’s flight, and the cabbage white is a common butterfly.
annotation.definitionFit: Cabbage whites are among the commonest fluttering butterflies, so many a flutter is one.

entries.clue: Divisive school is Mother Theresa’s first international college (10)

indicatorNotes.first: only the first letter of Theresa is used

blocks.note: sch. is the abbreviation for school

annotation.surface: A description of a controversial college, run in the name of Mother Teresa, that splits opinion.
annotation.walkthrough: Mother Theresa looks like one name; Mother is MA and Theresa gives only its T.
annotation.definitionFit: Schismatic means causing a schism, a split, so divisive.

entries.clue: See 10
Trainee mobile phone, yet complicated (8)

annotation.surface: A new employee struggling with a work mobile that is somehow still complicated.
annotation.walkthrough: Mobile phone reads as one thing; mobile is doing the job of shuffling, alongside complicated.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: neophyte, from the Greek for newly planted, is anyone new to a skill, as a trainee is.

entries.clue: Local gets in wrong rum (4-5)

indicatorNotes.rum: rum means odd, so the letters come out oddly arranged

blocks.note: to be in is to be at home

annotation.surface: The pub regular gets served the wrong spirit.
annotation.walkthrough: Local suggests a pub, and rum a drink; rum is the old British adjective for strange, which is the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: Home-grown produce or talent comes from the local area.

entries.clue: United takes sending off to be lacking certification (8)

indicatorNotes.off: letters that are off are out of order

blocks.note: U = United, as in football team names

annotation.surface: A football report: United have a player sent off.
annotation.walkthrough: Sending off is the football phrase for a red card; here the two words part company, sending as fodder and off as the signal.
annotation.definitionFit: A signature is what certifies a document or contract, so without one it goes uncertified.

entries.clue: Pure iodine added to a tobacco (8)

blocks.note: I is the chemical symbol for iodine

annotation.surface: A chemist’s note about lacing a tobacco blend with iodine.
annotation.walkthrough: Pure looks like a description of the iodine; it is VIRGIN, and the tobacco sits at the far end as the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Virginia is a type of tobacco, named after the American state where it was grown.

entries.clue: Low temperature? That’s debatable (4)

blocks.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do

annotation.surface: Someone questioning whether a reading on the thermometer is really low.
annotation.walkthrough: Low looks like an adjective about the weather; it is the verb for the noise a cow makes.
annotation.definitionFit: A moot point is one open to debate.

entries.clue: Mediocre elected president blocking measure (6)

indicatorNotes.blocking: the pair stands in the middle of the measure, as if blocking it

blocks.note: a tot is a small measure of spirits
a candidate who is elected gets in

annotation.surface: A second-rate leader, newly voted in, obstructing legislation.
annotation.walkthrough: Measure suggests a bill or policy; it is a tot, a small shot of drink.
annotation.definitionFit: Tinpot means inferior or second-rate, as in a tinpot dictator.

entries.clue: Exaggerating what a sewer might be doing (12)

annotation.definition2: what a sewer might be doing

blocks.note: to embroider a story is to add false detail

blocks.clueFragment: what a sewer might be doing
blocks.note: a sewer here is one who sews

annotation.surface: An overblown claim about what goes on in a drain.
annotation.walkthrough: A sewer reads as a drain; here it rhymes with grower and means someone who sews.
annotation.definitionFit: Embroidering means both decorating cloth with stitching and embellishing a tale.

entries.clue: One who regrets welcoming Latin dictator? (5)

annotation.surface: Someone with regrets taking in a Latin strongman.
annotation.walkthrough: Latin dictator looks like one phrase for a Roman or South American strongman; Latin supplies only its L.
annotation.definitionFit: A dictator is a ruler, and the question mark admits that not every ruler is a dictator.

entries.clue: Successor’s appearance reported (4)

indicatorNotes.reported: what is reported is heard, so the sound counts

blocks.note: an air is a look or manner

annotation.surface: A news item on how the heir to the throne looks.
annotation.walkthrough: The ’s reads as possessive; it is the word is, joining definition and wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: An heir is the one who succeeds to a title or estate.

entries.clue: Hot sort of scarf with neck opening (6)

indicatorNotes.opening: the opening of neck is its first letter

blocks.note: a stole is a long scarf worn over the shoulders

annotation.surface: A fashion note about a warm scarf with a slit for the neck.
annotation.walkthrough: Hot looks like temperature; it is slang for stolen goods.
annotation.definitionFit: A slang sense: hot goods are ones recently taken and still traceable, too risky to sell openly.

entries.clue: Maybe Burton’s ex at piano, learning rock intro (8)

indicatorNotes.intro: the intro of rock is its first letter

annotation.surface: Elizabeth Taylor, Richard Burton’s ex, at the piano learning rock.
annotation.walkthrough: Burton’s ex suggests the actor Richard Burton and Elizabeth Taylor; the Burton meant is Sir Richard Burton, the Victorian explorer.
annotation.definitionFit: Sir Richard Francis Burton was a Victorian explorer of Africa and Arabia; maybe marks him as one example.

entries.clue: One has copies, right, to correct and certify (8)

blocks.note: cc = carbon copies; has joins it on

annotation.surface: An office clerk who holds duplicates of documents, fixing and signing them off.
annotation.walkthrough: Has is the joining word that attaches CC to the one; the commas break the chain into its pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a body that accredits a school or lab formally vouches that it meets a standard.

entries.clue: Presidential term: ‘Career’s over in golf course support’ (6)

indicatorNotes.over: turned over, the word reads backwards
indicatorNotes.in: it goes inside the golf support

blocks.note: a tee holds the ball up on a golf course
a career is a run of work

annotation.surface: A headline declaring a president’s career finished while he is off playing golf.
annotation.walkthrough: Career’s over reads as a verdict on a politician; read the ’s as is, and over becomes the instruction to turn the career round.
annotation.definitionFit: Tenure is the period during which an office, such as a presidency, is held.
